summary: Iteration 39 (P0+P1 fixes + Feature #1 test-type chips + Feature #2 scheduled CSV email exports) is GREEN end-to-end. Backend: 13/13 pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_iter39_slots_and_csv_exports.py — both slot endpoints return 200 (tz bug fixed), full CSV-exports CRUD works (list/subscribe/idempotent-subscribe/unsubscribe), send-now returns the exact contract shape {ok,status,provider,to,kind} with no 500 (ZeptoMail 'error' status is EXPECTED, as documented), invalid kind rejected with 400/422, and front_desk role gets 403 on subscribe and send-now while still being able to list own subs. Frontend: (1) Test-type chip row renders on /patients/appointments with data-testid=appts-test-chips + PTA/SPEECH/IA/all chips showing counts. Clicking PTA adds ring-2 and filters table to 1 visible row. Row-level chip data-testid=appts-row-chip-APT-A8FF8C3E-2-PTA is clickable. Clicking `all` resets filter. (2) Book Appointment modal opens; DOM audit shows 0 <option> elements with <span> children out of 29 total options, and 0 hydration warnings containing 'cannot be a child of' + 'option' were emitted while opening the modal — the 11-pattern fix is verified. (3) EmailWeeklyCsvToggle renders on /patients/list (csv-weekly-toggle-patients + checkbox) and on /billing (csv-weekly-toggle-invoices + checkbox). Checking the box triggers POST /subscribe and reveals csv-weekly-send-now-{kind}; unchecking triggers DELETE and hides the button. Send-now click on invoices did not crash the page. Zero console errors and zero hydration warnings across all three pages.

critical_code_review_comments: csv_email_exports.py subscribe endpoint uses `existing.get('created_at')` inside the doc dict but reads it only when existing is truthy; the current code path is fine but the ternary is subtle — extract to a named var for readability.

SubscribeIn uses Literal['patients','invoices'] so invalid kinds return 422 (pydantic), not 400 as the docstring/manual check implies. This is fine — pytest accepts both — but consider adding a matching custom exception handler if you want a consistent 400 contract for all validation failures on this router.

send-now returns ok=(status in {sent,mocked}). Preview always returns status='error' so ok=False — UI should not treat this as a hard failure (currently the click didn't crash, but a toast reflecting the actual provider error would be a nicer UX).
